sentences.text: 3 These appeals are filed by the 6th respondent insurer in O.P (MV) Nos.1641 of 2004 and 1807 of 2004 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam.
The respondents herein are the claimants and respondents before the tribunal.

2. According to the claimants, on 28.12.2003 at about 04.00 pm while the claimants were travelling in a maruti car bearing registration No.KL-7-R-4410 driven by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner from south to north, an ambassador car bearing registration No.KA-19-M-6292 driven by the 4 th respondent in a negligent manner came from north to south and hit on the maruti car.
As a result of the accident, they had sustained serious injuries.
The claimants approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 2,00,000/- and 25,000/- respectively in each of the original petitions.
3. The first and second respondents, the driver and the owner of the offending maruti car remained ex parte before the tribunal.

The 3rd respondent, the insurer of the Maruti car, filed a written MACA NOs. 2572 OF 2012 & 649 of 2014 2025:KER:84355 statement denying the allegation of negligence on the part of the driver of the ambassador car and denying liability by contending that the policy issued was an Act Only policy.
The 4 th respondent is the driver and 5th respondent is the owner of the ambassador filed a written statement.

The 6th respondent, the insurer of the Ambassador car,
filed a written statement admitting the policy but disputing its liability to pay compensation.
Before the tribunal Exts.A1 to A10 and Ext. B1 were marked.
PW1 was examined.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 51,296/-(O.P(MV) No.1807 of 2004) and 8,245/- (O.P(MV) No.1641 of 2004) as compensation under different heads with interest @9% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from the 6 th respondent.
Challenging the liability to pay the amount awarded by the tribunal, the 6th respondent insurer of the ambassador car has come up in appeal.

4. Heard the learned standing counsel for the appellant, the learned standing counsel appearing for the 3 rd respondent and the learned counsel appearing for the 5 th respondent/owner of the ambassador.

Though notice was served on respondents 1 to 3 MACA NOs. 2572 OF 2012 & 649 of 2014 2025:KER:84355 (claimant as well as driver and owner of the maruthi car), they chose not to appear before this Court.

5. The learned standing counsel appearing for the appellant/insurance company submitted that they are mainly aggrieved by the finding of negligence on the part of the driver of the ambassador car, by the tribunal.
They relied on Exts.A1 to A10 which were produced by the claimants to prove their case.
Ext.A1 is the copy of the FIR, Ext.A3 is the copy of the charge sheet and Ext.A4 is the copy of the scene mahazar.

The learned standing counsel for the appellant further submitted that a charge sheet was drawn against the driver of the Maruti car, and a case was registered under Sections 279 and 337 of the IPC for rash and negligent driving of the said vehicle.
However, the driver of the Maruti car did not contest the charge sheet.

It is further submitted that the tribunal also went wrong in finding that the accident occurred 3.30 metres from the eastern tar end towards west and that the maruti car which was going from south to north was going on its right side and the tribunal wrongly found that the ambassador car had encroached onto the side of the maruti car, which is totally incorrect.

The appellant submitted that the road had a width of 7.60 metres, and the maruti MACA The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Kunjamma on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50933790/
4 NOs. 2572 OF 2012 & 649 of 2014 2025:KER:84355 car was proceeding from south to north, while the ambassador car was coming from north to south.

sentences.text: As per the scene mahazar, the point of impact was 3.30 metres from the eastern tar end towards the west, which is on the wrong side of the maruti van and the correct side of the ambassador car.
Hence, the finding of the tribunal that the maruti car was on its right side and that the ambassador car had encroached to the wrong side of the maruti car is incorrect.

6. The learned standing counsel appearing for the 4 th respondent/ insurance company submitted that the policy issued to the maruti car was an Act only Policy and the claimants have not claimed any compensation from the insurer of the car and have not alleged any negligence on the part of the driver of the maruti car.
7. On a perusal of the award as well as the documents produced, it is seen that the policy issued in respect of the maruti car was an Act only policy.
Ext. A4
scene mahazar also reveals that the spot of accident is 3.30 metres from the eastern tar end towards west.
Admittedly, the Maruti car was going from south to north and the ambassador car was moving in the direction, north to south.
The correct side of the ambassador car is the eastern side and the correct side of the Maruti car is western side.

Admittedly, there is no dispute MACA NOs. 2572 OF 2012 & 649 of 2014 2025:KER:84355 that the road was having a total width of 7.60 metres and the spot of accident is shown as 3.30 metres from the eastern tar end towards west.

The tribunal in paragraph 11 of the award, has mistakenly stated that though the spot of the accident was 3.30 metres from the eastern tar end towards the south, the maruti car was on its correct side and that the ambassador car had encroached onto the side of the maruti car.
This finding is totally incorrect.
Even as per the scene mahazar, it is evident that the maruti car had encroached into the right side of the ambassador car, thereby causing the accident.
Admittedly, the charge sheet is also drawn against the driver of the maruti car.
Hence, I do not find any reason for the tribunal to have found negligence on the part of the driver of the ambassador car and directed the appellant/6th respondent-insurer to pay the compensation.
PW1 has mounted the box and deposed that the ambassador car was driven at a high speed and that was the reason for causing the accident.
However, apart from his interested testimony, there is no other evidence or document to support the case of the claimants.
Though notice was served on the claimant, owner and driver of the maruti car they have chose not to appear before this court.
I find that the finding of the tribunal fastening the MACA NOs. 2572 OF 2012 & 649 of 2014 2025:KER:84355 liability upon the appellant-insurer is liable to be set aside.
Since the policy issued is an Act Only policy, the owner of the maruti car will be liable to pay the compensation awarded by the tribunal.
Accordingly both these appeals are allowed.

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed as follows:
The finding of the tribunal fastening the liability upon the appellant-insurer is liable hereby set aside.
The owner of the maruti car will be liable to pay the compensation awarded by the tribunal.
